address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore
w: Goodwood Park's Sichuan-Cantonese dining room since 1982 — one of Singapore's most respected Chinese restaurants (Frommer's), famous for its wood-fired Beijing duck carved at the table and served in two courses; refurbished in 2020 with Ernesto Bedmar interiors. Reviewed by critic Andy Hayler.

dish: Mao Shan Wang durian mousse cake and durian crêpes
n: Goodwood Park Hotel Coffee Lounge (durian desserts)
address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore
w: The hotel coffee lounge behind Singapore's best-known durian desserts: the Mao Shan Wang mousse cake, crêpes and Swiss rolls sold year-round and a seasonal all-you-can-eat durian dessert buffet each mid-year — covered annually by Eatbook and Time Out, and a long-running SGFoodOnFoot favourite.

dish: Hokkien popiah — juicy braised turnip, egg, prawn and crispy fish bits, finished with lard
address: #01-16 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495 (Makansutra prints #01-12 — unit to confirm)
w: A Hokkien popiah stall founded in 1930 and at Newton since 1977: fresh-wrapped rolls packed with juicy braised turnip, beansprouts, egg, prawn and crispy fish bits — one of the few non-seafood stalls Makansutra, Women's Weekly and Seth Lui all pick at Newton.

dish: French-Japanese plated desserts and entremets; Chef's Table dessert omakase
w: Pastry chef Makoto Arami (ex-executive pastry chef of Michelin-starred Béni and Marina Bay Sands) turned a 2021 online cult following into a black-and-white colonial bungalow off Scotts Road: a café of intricate Japanese-produce, French-technique pastries plus an eight-seat dessert-omakase room — covered by Tatler, The Peak, ladyironchef and SGFoodOnFoot.

dish: Cantonese private-dining course menu — abalone, roast pork, wagyu
w: An eight-seat Cantonese private-dining room near Newton serving course menus built on abalone, pork and wagyu — listed in Eatbook's Newton guide and reviewed by SGFoodOnFoot (2024).
